issues.failure_explanation: A continuous embedding B1 into H1 yields only H1-boundedness; combined with Rellich it yields L2-convergent subsequences, never H1-convergent ones. The first assertion is in fact false: on Ω=(0,1) the k-tooth sawtooth functions of height 1/k (slope ±1 on teeth of width 1/k) are ReLU networks with uniformly bounded Barron norm (each tooth is a combination of three normalized ridges with O(1) coefficients, and there are O(k) teeth averaged over O(k) neurons), yet ||f_k'||_{L2} ≡ 1 while f_k → 0 in L2, so no subsequence converges in H1.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 2 states no hypothesis on r(n), and the prose advertises 'without requiring additional conditions on r(n)'. The proof, however, needs r(n) ≥ c_ρ(f†) eventually (it uses the generalized inverse r^{-1}(c_ρ(f†)) in N2 and asserts r(n) → +∞, a property appearing nowhere in the hypotheses). If r is bounded above by a value below c_ρ(f†), the approximating networks of Proposition Approximtion theorem, which lie in X_{n,c_ρ(f†)}, are inadmissible; since A is injective and X_{n,r(n)} compact, min over the class of ||A(f)−g|| stays bounded below by a positive constant, so the discrepancy test J > τδ never passes for small δ, the loop never terminates, and k(δ) < ∞ together with the convergence claim fail.

issues.failure_explanation: c_{ρ_n}(f) is computed from a particular coefficient tuple, but the same function in X_{n,∞} admits many tuples with different values of (1/n)Σ|a_i|(‖b_i‖₁+|c_i|); e.g. the constant function v on [0,1] has cost |v| with the n-tuple a_i = v, b_i = 0, c_i = 1, but cost n|v| with the tuple a_1 = nv, a_2 = … = 0, b_1 = 0, c_1 = 1. The proofs also conflate the two objects: the identity φ(‖f_{n,k}‖_{B1}) = P(f_{n,k}) used in (b) is false (only ≤ holds, via the infimum definition of the Barron norm), so the existence/stability arguments are only valid after fixing a representing tuple.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
According to \cite{Deng2023,Fleischer1999}, the auto-convolution operator is not injective (e.g.\ $A(f)=A(-f)$).
However, when restricted to the cone of strictly nonnegative functions (e.g.\ $f\in C[0,1]$ with $f>0$),

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims Example 2 satisfies the assumptions of Theorems 1–2, whose convergence proofs conclude f* = f† by invoking injectivity of A at the limit of the iterates. The auto-convolution operator satisfies A(f) = A(−f) (the paper cites this itself), and the search classes X_{n,r(n)} of Algorithms 1–2 contain sign-changing networks and are symmetric under f ↦ −f; no cone restriction is imposed in the algorithm or in the experiment. Hence the injectivity hypothesis fails on the class over which the algorithms minimize, both f† and −f† are admissible limits consistent with the discrepancy principle, and the claimed regularization guarantee does not cover this example as stated.

failure_location.quote: Thus, $A$ is locally Lipschitz at any $f^\dagger\in H^1(\Omega)$, and Example~\ref{Ex2} meets the assumptions of Theorems~1-2.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the admissible class to nonnegative networks (a closed, compactness-preserving subset that still contains the nonnegative exact solution) and invoke the theorems with A restricted to that cone.
issues.overall_effect: The assertion that Example 2 is covered by Theorems 1–2 (and the empirical validation of those theorems via this example) is unsupported; the regularization guarantee can fail on the stated search class.
issues.title: Example 2's claimed compliance with Theorems 1–2 is false: A is not injective on the class searched by the algorithms
issues.why_classification: A substantive restriction of the algorithm's feasible class is required and a stated compliance claim is withdrawn, although a comparable, theoretically covered version of the example survives; more than a local routine fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The only estimate established is the L^∞-based bound ‖Λ_f − Λ_{f†}‖ ≤ C‖f − f†‖_{L^∞(Ω)}. Converting it to the claimed H^1-based bound would require the embedding H^1(Ω) ↪ L^∞(Ω), which is false for the two-dimensional domain Ω = [0,1]² (H^1 embeds into L^q for every q < ∞ but not L^∞). diagnostic_evidence.quote: Moreover, instead of using a complete data $\{(h,g): g= \Lambda_f(h)\}$, we only use a sample of data $(h_1, g_1=\Lambda_f(h_1))$ with

It is well established that the DN map uniquely determines an isotropic, essentially bounded conductivity. Consequently, the forward operator  $A: f\mapsto\Lambda_f$ is injective at $f^\dagger$ \cite{AstalaPaivarinta2006}.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that one boundary-measurement pair suffices 'for the current model problem'. The injectivity established in the source concerns the complete Dirichlet-to-Neumann map Λ_f; the operator actually used in the experiment is the single-pair map f ↦ Λ_f(h₁), for which injectivity is neither proved nor known in general (single-measurement Calderón-type problems are non-unique in this generality). The paper therefore claims theoretical coverage of its EIT experiment that it never establishes.

failure_location.quote: It is worth noting that, although a single measurement pair is sufficient for the current model problem, employing multiple sets of boundary measurements (e.g., 20 pairs derived from different voltage patterns) provides additional data and can lead to slightly improved reconstruction accuracy.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the claim to state that the single-pair experiment is illustrative, with uniqueness guaranteed only for the complete DN map; alternatively, prove injectivity of the single-pair operator on the admissible conductivity class.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the single-pair experiment instantiates the paper's regularization theory is materially misleading; only the full-DN-map operator is covered by the theory.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that a single boundary-measurement pair suffices for the EIT inverse problem
issues.why_classification: A local, scoped qualification of the prose preserves every formal result, guarantee, and the experimental content; nothing substantive is lost.
